summary: Improvement remains pointed at the right outcome and the current top-priority order still matches the full product stack. The most important learning since yesterday is that no new internal evidence has displaced the 2026-03-25 shift in Priority 3 from first-use activation to repeated-use sufficiency: the second-cycle overnight-ledger evidence still holds as the main live proof surface, while Priority 1 remains the structural bottleneck and Priority 2 remains the clearest unchanged deployment gap. Net result: learn-and-replan completed with no material priority reordering, no justified deeper research, and TOP_PRIORITIES.md confirmed current rather than refreshed.
materialChanges: No new internal product-surface change since the 2026-03-25 overnight cycle materially altered Improvement direction, bottleneck order, or next-step framing.

The latest internal delta remains the already-incorporated 2026-03-25 repeated-cycle overnight-ledger evidence and stuckness check, which continues to support Priority 3 as a live control-proof surface rather than a future-only design item.
Current runtime/task surfaces still show OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069 open, so Priority 1 remains the strongest structural bottleneck in lived execution rather than a solved substrate question.
A-005 pinned-lane migration still shows no new delivery-path evidence; interim-drift exposure therefore remains materially unchanged.

External scan surfaced only weak general reinforcement for auditability and digital audit trails, not a product-shaping change. External delta disposition remains watch/no_material_change rather than update_now.

topPriorities.nextStep: Implement the pinned lane as an operational path with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-drift gap.

topPriorities.why: Improvement now owns the minimum standard for proving whether recurring loops ran, helped, and remain auditable. The key live uncertainty is no longer first-use activation but whether repeated cycles stay inspectable and honest without needing heavier task-layer representation too early.
topPriorities.currentStatus: The 2026-03-25 repeated-cycle sufficiency and anti-stuckness evidence remains the freshest live proof. The compact selected-priority -> intake/current-work -> ledger -> execution-evidence chain held across a second cycle, and the next-cycle escalation rule is explicit. No new evidence since then changes this framing.
topPriorities.nextStep: Reuse and maintain the compact canonical ledger path on future overnight cycles only while each reuse produces comparably explicit bounded advancement; escalate to stronger task-layer representation if a later cycle stops meeting that standard cleanly.
